description: A materials operations manager must decide the disposition and recovery controls for 1,200 electric-motor housings exposed to water in finished-goods storage, with input from quality and warehouse supervision.

shared_context.S1: A roof leak exposed 1,200 electric-motor housings in finished-goods storage overnight.
shared_context.S2: The housings are arranged as four pallets of 300 units each, labeled P1, P2, P3, and P4.
shared_context.S3: The customer's Monday assembly schedule depends on the housings, and the materials operations manager has authority to release, hold, or scrap the affected stock.
shared_context.S4: The plant's standard process is to hold a quality-and-warehouse disposition huddle before any water-exposed material is released or discarded; at the start of the huddle, quality and warehouse each state their current recorded finding, after which the manager summarizes the agreed disposition and issues the formal decision.

PF1.text: Jon's electrical laboratory report, pending his sign-off before upload to the quality system, covers the 600 housings on P2 and P4: 540 passed insulation testing and 60 failed; the 540 passing units may be released only after 100% insulation testing is recorded, while the 60 failed units must be scrapped.

PF2.text: Elena's warehouse inspection log, awaiting inventory reconciliation, identifies P2 and P4 as the only pallets that received direct water exposure; the 600 units on those pallets correspond to Jon's tested lot, and the dry room can process them in exactly 6 hours before release, so P2 and P4 must remain segregated during drying.

acceptance_conditions: Pallets P2 and P4 must be held and segregated during recovery.
The exposed material must receive exactly 6 hours of dry-room processing.
100% insulation testing must be required before release.
A dry-room recovery commitment must be recorded.

decisive_facts.why: The laboratory result changes the disposition to exactly 1,140 released units and 60 scrapped units and changes the plan to require 100% insulation testing before release.
The warehouse inspection changes the affected pallet assignment to exactly P2 and P4 and changes recovery to a segregated dry-room process lasting exactly 6 hours with a recorded recovery commitment.
